meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 9: MCP Inspector (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about the MCP Inspector are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A server that passes Inspector checks is proven conformant for any host
It can run as a web app, a CLI or a TUI, with the web client as the default
Passing both --catalog and --config is rejected by all three clients
The CLI can hold a subscriptions/listen stream open between invocations
The web UI listens on port 6274 and protects its API with a session token

questions.explanation: A, B and C are documented. Passing the Inspector narrows the fault domain but does not prove every host integration detail, and stream- or session-only methods are rejected by the CLI because a process that exits cannot hold a stream open.

questions.question: Your CI step fails. Which of these are things the Inspector CLI actually gives you for diagnosis? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A stable exit code per failure class
A replay file that re-runs the exact session offline
A single JSON error line on stderr, parseable with jq
--format json output with no banners, for piping into jq
A conformance score for the server, from 0 to 100

questions.explanation: Exit codes, the one-line JSON error envelope on stderr and clean JSON output are the CLI's scripting surface. There is no replay file and no conformance score.
